## Texas Senate polling checkpoint — October 14, 2026

**Resolution rule:** This is a question about **Race to the WH’s Paxton–Talarico general-election polling average on October 31**, not who wins the November 3 election. A tie would not satisfy “Paxton leads.”

**Resolution sources first:** Both specified Race to the WH pages are accessible. The polling page says its average gives greater weight to recent polls, larger samples, and pollsters with strong track records; the Senate forecast page embeds a polling graphic. **Neither page exposes the selected Texas matchup’s numerical average in the text available to me, so I cannot verify its current Paxton–Talarico figure or leader directly.** The Texas race page confirms Paxton and Talarico are the nominees. Do not substitute another site’s average for the figure that will resolve this question. ([racetothewh.com](https://www.racetothewh.com/senate/26))

**Most recent polling and status quo:**
- **October 14:** Marist released a survey fielded **October 8–11** showing **Talarico 47%, Paxton 45%** among likely voters (±4.9-point margin of error). ([maristpoll.marist.edu](https://maristpoll.marist.edu/polls/2026-midterm-elections-in-texas-october-2026/))
- **October 13:** The University of Texas/Texas Politics Project released a survey fielded **September 25–October 5** showing **Talarico 50%, Paxton 47%** among likely voters (±3.34 points). ([texaspolitics.utexas.edu](https://texaspolitics.utexas.edu/blog/latest-ut-texas-politics-poll-finds-historic-levels-of-competition-in-texas-midterm-elections))
- As a **cross-check, not the resolution measure**, RealClearPolling currently lists **Talarico 48.1%, Paxton 45.5%**, a 2.6-point lead, across polls dated September 18–October 11. Its listed recent polls include a tie, but none with Paxton ahead. ([realclearpolling.com](https://www.realclearpolling.com/elections/senate/2026/texas))

**Historical context:** Republicans won the last three Texas U.S. Senate general elections—**2018, 2020, and 2024**—so the recent Democratic polling leads depart from the state’s recent election results. That **0-for-3 Democratic election record is not a base rate for the narrower event of leading a particular polling average on October 31**; the current polls are more directly relevant to that event. ([fec.gov](https://www.fec.gov/resources/cms-content/documents/federalelections2018.pdf?utm_source=openai))

**Before resolution:** Texas in-person early voting runs **October 19–30**. Polls released or added through **October 31** could change Race to the WH’s weighted average; its recency weighting also matters as existing polls age. Election Day is **November 3**, *after* this polling checkpoint. ([sos.state.tx.us](https://www.sos.state.tx.us/elections/candidates/guide/2026/dates2026.shtml?utm_source=openai))

**Would it resolve Yes or No on current information?** The independently visible polling points to **No**—Talarico, not Paxton, leads—but **the exact resolution-source average is unverified**. I would not record a definitive current-site resolution without checking the Texas matchup inside Race to the WH’s interactive graphic. ([realclearpolling.com](https://www.realclearpolling.com/elections/senate/2026/texas))

**Sources:**
- [1](https://www.racetothewh.com/senate/26)
- [2](https://maristpoll.marist.edu/polls/2026-midterm-elections-in-texas-october-2026/)
- [3](https://texaspolitics.utexas.edu/blog/latest-ut-texas-politics-poll-finds-historic-levels-of-competition-in-texas-midterm-elections)
- [4](https://www.realclearpolling.com/elections/senate/2026/texas)
- [5](https://www.fec.gov/resources/cms-content/documents/federalelections2018.pdf?utm_source=openai)
- [6](https://www.sos.state.tx.us/elections/candidates/guide/2026/dates2026.shtml?utm_source=openai)

criterios: This question resolves as Yes if as of October 31, 2026, Ken Paxton leads James Talarico in the General Election Polling Average at the 2026 Senate Polling tracker at the [RaceToTheWH](https://www.racetothewh.com/senate/26) website.

INSTRUCTIONS: At the resolution link, scroll down to Polling Average. Then select the race under Choose a State & Matchup.

An alternate link at the resolution source is https://www.racetothewh.com/senate/26polls
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** 16 days, until October 31, 2026.  
(b) **Status quo:** Available recent polls and a separate polling average show Talarico ahead. Race to the WH’s exact Paxton–Talarico average has not been verified.  
(c) **Reference class:** As a rough forecasting benchmark, I would expect a candidate trailing a polling average by roughly 2–3 points with two weeks left to take the lead only a minority of the time—perhaps 10–20%. This is a judgmental range, not a measured historical rate.  
(d) **No scenario:** New polls remain close or favor Talarico, leaving him ahead in the specified average.  
(e) **Yes scenario:** Late polls favor Paxton strongly enough to move Race to the WH’s weighted average into a Paxton lead by October 31.  
(f) **Technicality:** Only the **Paxton–Talarico general-election polling average on Race to the WH** decides this. A tie, a lead on another site, or a later election victory does not count.

Probability: 15%

(a) There are about 16 days left. The question resolves on Race to the WH's Texas polling average as of October 31, 2026.

(b) If nothing changed, the answer would be No. Every visible recent poll has Talarico ahead or tied:
- Marist, October 8–11: Talarico +2.
- UT/Texas Politics Project, September 25–October 5: Talarico +3.
- RealClearPolling average: Talarico +2.6, with no recent poll showing Paxton ahead.

Race to the WH weights recent, large-sample, high-quality polls, so its average very likely also shows Talarico ahead, probably by 2–3 points. I could not verify that figure directly.

(c) The reference class is a polling-average leader about two weeks before the measurement date. Leads of 2–3 points in an average flip within about 2 weeks perhaps 15–25% of the time. Late tightening toward Republicans in Texas, possibly helped by a late wave of Republican-leaning pollsters, makes a flip somewhat more plausible than usual.

(d) No scenario: Late polls, released during early voting, keep showing Talarico narrowly ahead or tied, and the weighted average stays Talarico +1 to +3 through October 31.

(e) Yes scenario: Several late polls show Paxton ahead, from Republican-leaning firms or from a genuine shift as partisans come home. The recency weighting then pulls the average to Paxton by a small margin by October 31.

(f) Technicalities:
- A tie resolves No.
- Only Race to the WH's own average counts. It could differ from RealClearPolling if it includes different pollsters or uses different weights.
- I could not see the current Race to the WH number, so there is a small chance it already differs from the other averages.

Probability: 17%

(a) **Time left:** 16 days until October 31, 2026.
(b) **Status quo outcome:** No (James Talarico currently holds an estimated ~2.5-point lead across recent high-quality surveys such as Marist and UT/Texas Politics Project, making Talarico the expected leader in the RaceToTheWH average as well).
(c) **Reference class and base rate:** Senate candidates trailing by 2 to 3 points in polling averages 16 days before the checkpoint/election in states where the underlying partisan fundamentals favor them. Polling averages flip within a ~2-week span in roughly 20–25% of such cases, as aggregate averages lag and require multiple decisive polls to reverse.
(d) **Scenario resulting in No:** Incoming surveys in late October continue to show Talarico holding a 1- to 3-point lead or effectively tied, buoyed by Paxton's high personal unfavorability ratings. With insufficient time and polls to fully erase Talarico's existing lead, RaceToTheWH maintains Talarico ahead on October 31.
(e) **Scenario resulting in Yes:** Republican voters consolidate behind Paxton during the opening week of early voting, producing several new high-rated polls showing Paxton up by 2 to 4 points. RaceToTheWH's recency weighting rapidly moves Paxton into the lead by October 31.
(f) **Technicalities:** The resolution specifically requires Ken Paxton to *lead* Talarico in the RaceToTheWH General Election Polling Average on October 31, 2026. An exact tie resolves to No. The actual election outcome on November 3 is irrelevant; only the snapshot on RaceToTheWH on October 31 matters.

Probability: 24%
